method: Representative whole-fruit mass in grams; one fruit including skin and seeds. Cultivar-specific measured averages, published typical values, market grades and range midpoint estimates are distinguished. This is a game ranking dataset, not global species means or a claim that weight equals geometric size.

Cherry.note: Stella sweet cherry accession, UK National Fruit Collection fruit-weight record; one cherry, despite paired artwork.

Redcurrant.note: Rovada: mean of five annual berry means (0.8, 0.7, 0.7, 0.4, 0.6 g), WARC 2017–2021.

Blackcurrant.note: Lithuanian cultivar trial, 2005–2008 grand mean 134.1 g per 100 berries; divided by 100.

Gooseberry.note: Ribes grossularia, Kestel/Bursa trial; reported mean fruit weight.

Acerola.note: Mean across 103 Brazilian phenotypes; observed range 1.53–8.85 g.

Raspberry.note: Unweighted mean of 15 reported cultivar × year × field/tunnel cell means (2019–2020); not a production-weighted species average.

Persimmon.note: Fuyu cultivar, reported fruit weight in Florida trial.

Jackfruit.note: Black Gold representative medium cultivar, 22 lb × 453.59237 g/lb. Cultivars vary greatly.

Blueberry.note: Missouri cultivar trial, mean of 13 cultivated highbush blueberry cultivars (2011–2016).

Blackberry.note: Missouri cultivar trial, mean of 14 cultivated blackberry cultivars (2011–2016).

Bilberry.note: Midpoint of reported 0.28–0.32 g annual means for wild Vaccinium myrtillus in central Bosnia.

Cranberry.note: Mullica Queen representative cultivar, published average berry weight.

Cloudberry.note: Nine female clones in Bench 1; reported mean 1.69 g/berry.

Salmonberry.note: Martindale and Jurakic archaeological reconstruction estimate, not a measured population mean.

Mulberry.note: Purple-fruited 46CO19 cultivar, inventor-reported mean; representative cultivated mulberry.

Pineberry.note: Florida Pearl FL 16.78-109; midpoint of patent’s 16–20 g average fruit-weight range.

Strawberry.note: Medallion cultivar, 0.5 lb/acre/day early nitrogen treatment; reported whole-season mean.

Coffee cherry.note: Midpoint of 10.8–27.2 g per 10 fresh cherries, divided by 10; selected coffee trees, not beans.

Chokeberry.note: Viking control cultivar; reported mean of one fruit (not a cluster).

Grapes.note: Fantasy Seedless: midpoint of typical 6–8 g per berry. Artwork is a bunch; ranking uses ONE grape for consistency.

Rambutan.note: Arka Coorg Arun; midpoint of 40–45 g fruit range.

Mangosteen.note: Grower’s 2006 sample of 32 whole purple mangosteens; about 4 oz average, including rind.

Boysenberry.note: Boysen clone 43, early-season ripe fruit in 1994 trial, 50 fruit.

Langsat.note: Nilgiris study, Table 2 whole-fruit mean. Component means in the paper do not sum to this total; use reported whole-fruit value, lower confidence.

Salak.note: Unweighted mean of Mawar plants Mwr-1 through Mwr-7 (43.54, 41.03, 47.70, 42.32, 38.55, 24.74, 24.00 g); selected group, not all salak.

Mandarin.note: Satsuma representative: midpoint of reported 139–154 g mean fruit weights across scion/rootstock combinations.

Blood orange.note: Moro representative cultivar, reported mean whole-fruit weight.

Kumquat.note: Midpoint of published 5–20 g range for Fortunella margarita; range estimate, not a population mean.

Lychee.note: Shahi representative cultivar, midpoint of 22–26 g fruit weights.

Longan.note: Taiwan cultivar-characterization research abstract; 5.2–18.2 g observed range, mean 10.6 g.

Key lime.note: Nueva Vizcaya State University citrus accession; recorded fruit weight.

Calamansi.note: Midpoint of 6.15–17.02 g germplasm range; estimate, not the study mean.

Apricot.note: Bergeron representative cultivar, reported mean fruit weight.

Feijoa.note: Twelve cultivars in southern Italy; reported 73.0 ± 16.7 g average over three years.

Apple.note: Red Velox representative red apple, 2016–2020 reported average.

Green apple.note: Granny Smith representative green apple, 2016–2020 reported average.

Golden apple.note: Golden Delicious Reinders representative yellow apple (Malus domestica, not ambarella), 2016–2020 average.

Wax apple.note: Thai Department of Agricultural Extension Java apple/Syzygium samarangense: midpoint of 100–150 g whole-fruit range.

Golden kiwi.note: Waikato gold-kiwifruit sample, Table 3.1 reported mean mass; cultivar/sample-specific.

Kiwifruit.note: Hayward representative green kiwifruit; midpoint of published 60–90 g fruit range.

Quince.note: Midpoint of horticultural reference average-weight range 100–280 g; not a measured global mean.

Jujube.note: Iranian Ziziphus jujuba accessions; fresh-fruit grand mean, not dry weight. Larger cultivated varieties exist.

Loquat.note: Mkarkeb representative cultivar, measured mature fruit mean.

Mirabelle.note: Mirabelle in THDC Mustang, 2022, Table 5 average whole-fruit weight.

Cherimoya.note: 448 fruits from 137 trees, Loja Ecuador characterization; reported average 400 g.

Custard apple.note: Interpreted as Annona reticulata (bullock’s heart), distinct from cherimoya; FAO typical fruit about 300 g.

Mango.note: Tommy Atkins representative cultivar, average weight of the parent in the cited hybrid population.

Dragonfruit.note: Midpoint of reported average-weight range 350–450 g for Hylocereus fruit in US production review.

Papaya.note: Red Lady representative large commercial papaya; ministry production manual average 1.8 kg.

Tamarillo.note: Unweighted mean of Amber 90 g, Laird’s Large 108 g and Mulligan 44 g raw whole-fruit means.

Coconut.note: Ghana hybrid coconut sample, whole fresh fruit including husk and shell: 1.68 kg. Artwork depicts a dehusked coconut; ranking still uses botanical whole fruit.

Cacao.note: Whole fresh pod reconstructed as mean husk 355.82 g + mean seeds/pulp 121.72 g; not a cocoa bean.

Citron.note: Nueva Vizcaya State University Citrus medica accession; recorded fruit weight (not French citron/lemon).

Pomelo.note: 2024 harvest of 410 whole fruits, reported average 1.45 kg.

Durian.note: Sua Hat Lep representative cultivar, midpoint of 2.5–2.7 kg average-weight range.

Pawpaw.note: North American Asimina triloba, not papaya; review mean of cultivar averages from 61 cultivars, not production-weighted.

Melon.note: Seed supplier comparison chart; Athena cantaloupe, 5–6 lb. Pounds converted to grams.

Galia melon.note: Seed supplier comparison chart; Arava, 3–4 lb. Pounds converted to grams.

Canary melon.note: Seed supplier comparison chart; Brilliant, 4 lb average. Pounds converted to grams.

Piel de Sapo.note: Seed supplier comparison chart; Lambkin, 3 lb average. Pounds converted to grams.

Crenshaw melon.note: Seed supplier comparison chart; Lilly, 6–8 lb. Pounds converted to grams.

Snow Leopard melon.note: Seed supplier comparison chart; Snow Leopard, 2 lb average. Pounds converted to grams.

Hami melon.note: Dongfangmi 3 cultivar release; reported average single-fruit weight 2.0 kg.

Korean melon.note: Authors’ physical analysis table, 14 Korean melons in harvesting-tool study; reported mean.

Watermelon.note: Crimson Sweet representative red watermelon, reported mean across early and full cropping seasons.

Sugar Baby watermelon.note: Sugar Baby, JICA cultivation guide reported average 4 kg.

Winter melon.note: Benincasa hispida; grower-reported 15–20 lb average range, midpoint converted to grams.

Butternut.note: Waltham Butternut; midpoint of seed supplier 4–5 lb average range.

Acorn squash.note: Table Queen; midpoint of grower/supplier 1.25–2 lb average range.

Yuzu.note: UC Riverside evaluation 2003–2007, Riverside and Lindcove: mean weight per fruit 52 g.

Casaba melon.note: Golden Beauty: seed conservation association’s 2000–3000 g fruit range, midpoint.

Red pineapple.note: Ananas bracteatus var. albus proxy for red/wild pineapple; measured 30-fruit sample with crowns. Not an exact measurement of the illustrated red cultivar.

Yellow watermelon.note: Yellow Doll representative yellow-fleshed cultivar; midpoint of breeder’s 5–7 lb average range.

Huckleberry.note: Vaccinium membranaceum; overall fresh-fruit mean across sampled locations and years.

Damson.note: Shropshire Prune/Damson accession, UK National Fruit Collection fruit-weight record.

Greengage.note: Reine Claude/Greengage accession, UK National Fruit Collection fruit-weight record.

Plum.note: Stanley European plum representative, study mean fruit mass.

Guava.note: Allahabad Safeda, integrated-nutrient treatment T5 study mean; sample-specific.

Bergamot.note: Fantastico representative cultivar at March harvest; mean across two harvest years.

Crabapple.note: Mean of two measured whole-fruit genotype means, 46 EL 01 (17.31 g) and 46 EL 02 (12.53 g).

Starfruit.note: B2/MAHA 66 representative cultivar, midpoint of 160–220 g medium-fruit range.

Pineapple.note: Kew/Smooth Cayenne representative cultivar; midpoint of 2–3 kg whole-fruit range.

Pepino.note: Solanum muricatum; midpoint of published typical 80–250 g whole-fruit range.

Cactus pear.note: Cultivated Opuntia fruit; midpoint of published 75–250 g whole-fruit range.

Nectarine.note: Nectaross representative cultivar, reported mean 170 ± 10 g.

Avocado.note: Hass, Tenerife study grand mean whole-fruit weight 239 ± 54 g.

Clementine.note: Nueva Vizcaya State University clementine accession; recorded whole-fruit weight.

Pale striped watermelon.note: Artwork colour description, not a defined cultivar. Shares the Crimson Sweet striped-watermelon 6.01 kg measured mean; no invented size difference.

Lemon.note: Eureka SL representative cultivar; NSW DPI fruit-quality evaluation average whole-fruit weight.

Passionfruit.note: Ripe purple passionfruit: midpoint of Kerala Farm Information Bureau’s typical 35–45 g fruit range.

Jabuticaba.note: MC-05-06 representative clone; midpoint of reported average-fruit-weight range 4.02–7.0 g in USDA characterization abstract.

Breadfruit.note: Cultivar evaluation thesis: reported mean whole-fruit weight 1.2 kg across cultivars and study years.

Pumpkin.note: Small Sugar culinary pumpkin representative; midpoint of 5–6 lb range, excludes giant competition pumpkins.

Loganberry.note: Polish 2007–2008 trial: 494 g per 100 fruits, divided by 100.

Pear.note: Bartlett representative, nonthinned treatment in 1993, eight trees; yield divided by fruit count.

Asian pear.note: Hosui representative, reported 250 g cultivar mean from Carolina trial summarized in RNR Journal.

Fig.note: Brown Turkey representative, reported fresh individual-fruit weight.

Sapodilla.note: PKM 1 representative cultivar; National Horticulture Board average fruit weight.

Honeydew.note: Green Flesh representative cultivar; midpoint of supplier 1.5–2.4 kg range. Use metric figures; parenthetical pound equivalents are approximate.

Kabocha.note: Sweet Mama green-skinned kabocha, supplier typical 1.3 kg fruit.

Orange watermelon.note: Orangeglo representative cultivar; midpoint of observed trial yields 15–20 lb fruit, not packet’s larger 20–30 lb description.

Lime.note: Persian lime representative cultivar; Pakistan citrus characterization average, whole fruit.

Pomegranate.note: Wonderful representative cultivar; midpoint of reported two-season average-weight range 304.5–337.38 g.

Star apple.note: Chrysophyllum cainito (not African star apple): equal mean of green 136.40 g and purple 150.78 g cultivar means, Table 1.

Soursop.note: Soconusco, Chiapas accession study, Table 2 grand mean whole-fruit weight; large accession variation.

Peach.note: Redhaven on Rootpac-40, 2017–2023 average whole-fruit weight; representative orchard combination.

Rose apple.note: Syzygium jambos, fruit-selection study: 27 whole fruits, mean 22.1 ± 5.88 g; distinct from wax apple.

Medlar.note: Nottingham representative cultivar, Dutch Research Station for Fruit Growing 1985 trial, 24 g fruit weight.

Tangerine.note: USDA Food Buying Guide: 120-count whole fresh tangerines, four whole fruit per purchased pound; 453.59237/4. A commercial size grade, not peeled portion mass.

Ugli fruit.note: USDA Food Buying Guide: one whole 32-count ugli fruit ≈14.6 oz; ×28.349523125 g/oz. Commercial grade, not a global cultivar average.
